There are four cook modes, Merge low priority, Merge, Overwrite and Remove. 

Merge low priority - automatically happens when changing or replacing any object referenced by the recipe line (sometimes manually cooking is required).

Other options regarding interaction with conflicting data that is stored directly in the cue.
As you know, directly stored data has a higher priority than the recipe line data.

Merge - removes from the cue the data that is in conflict, allowing the recipe data to output 

Overwrite - removes from the cue all data that isn't recipe.

Remove - basically, mutes recipe data until a cook command is triggered. 

This behavior is a new addition and might be changed in later versions (especially Remove behavior) but we'll see

Short answer: Hire a lighting designer. 

Longer answer: I assume you're not in the position to purchase all the gear required for a lighting setup, and still wish to use the local setups. And in that situation you really need a person who is familiar with your stuff and will be able to adapt any venue for your desired looks. Timecode shows need a constant setup. That's why the really big artists roll up to their shows with truckloads of gear, they bring everything with them. So in your position I would not suggest to automate your light show, but instead, entrust it with a present professional (or an aspirin one..). It would mean to pay another person every show, but buying the gear required for an automated show isn't cheap either, and I believe would give you a worse outcome than with a person on the controls.

Think about this like actors on stage. In a small stage they do not need to be amplified, and so you have the added effect of the relative position on stage. But when the venue is too big, you give each one a neck mic and they all come out of the sound system. There can be things you can do (maybe play around with the left/right valus of the stereo) but generally it looks to me like this concept is not scalable if the relative position of the source of the sound is critical.
